subject: Game Theory
title: The Stable Marriage Problem
description: A fast breakdown of The Stable Marriage Problem for builders.

hook.text: Ten men and ten women each rank each other. Can we match them so nobody prefers someone else's partner over theirs?

buildup.text: An unstable match has a 'blocking pair': two people who'd rather be with each other than their assigned partners.

discovery.text: Gale and Shapley proved stable matchings always exist. Their algorithm: one side proposes, the other accepts or rejects.

twist.text: The proposing side gets their best stable partner. The accepting side gets their worst. Who proposes matters enormously.

climax.text: Lloyd Shapley won the 2012 Nobel Prize for this work. The algorithm now matches doctors, students, and organ donors.

punchline.text: The right match needs the right process.

quiz.question: What makes a matching 'stable'?
options: No pair prefers each other over assigned partners
